questions.question: Container queries let a component respond to:

options.text: The size of its CONTAINER, not the viewport

questions.explanation: Unlike media queries (viewport-based), container queries adapt a component to its parent's width — true component-driven responsiveness.

questions.question: Before a container query can target an element, you must:

options.text: Set container-type: inline-size (or size) on an ANCESTOR

questions.explanation: container-type establishes an element as a query container; @container then queries its size. The query container is the ancestor, not the element itself.

questions.question: The syntax to apply styles based on container width is:
questions.explanation: @container queries the nearest ancestor container. This is the modern replacement for hacky viewport-based component styling.

questions.question: The main advantage over media queries is:

options.text: A component restyles correctly wherever it's placed (sidebar, main, card) without knowing the viewport

questions.explanation: Components become self-adapting to their context, enabling true reusable UI — a big win for design systems.

questions.question: container-type: inline-size vs size differs in that:

options.text: inline-size queries only the inline (width) axis; size allows both dimensions but blocks size containment

questions.explanation: inline-size (most common) containers query width cheaply. size enables block-axis queries but applies size containment (children can't affect container size).

questions.question: Can you name a container for targeted queries?
questions.explanation: container-name lets you scope @container to a named container, useful when multiple containers exist.

questions.question: Container queries are especially valuable for:

options.text: Reusable design-system components placed in varying layouts

questions.explanation: Components (cards, widgets) that appear in sidebars, grids, and modals benefit most — they adapt to placement, not viewport.

questions.question: For older browsers without support, you should:

options.text: Provide a sensible default (viewport media query / base styles) as fallback

questions.explanation: Progressive enhancement: default layout works without container queries; @supports can gate advanced styling.
